chunks: 362 - A group of scholars narrated to me on the authority of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya in the city of peace (al-Salam), who said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khallan narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather 'Attab, from the descendants of 'Attab ibn Umayd, who said: The successor - Mahdi (peace be upon him) was born on Friday, and his mother is Raihana, and she is called Narjis, and she is called Saiqal, and she is called Susan, except that it was said due to the pregnancy that she was called Saiqal.
ai.seo_question: Who is the mother of the Mahdi (a.s.) and what are her names according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the Friday birth of Imam al-Mahdi, linking it to the auspicious day of creation and resurrection in Shia eschatology. It highlights the multi-nominal identity of his mother, Raihana (Narjis), with 'Saiqal' (shining) specifically denoting the spiritual luminosity of her pregnancy, a detail often cited in biographical dictionaries to affirm her purity and status.
